topic: The Origin and Color Dependence of the Index of Refraction

sections.title: Hook & Prerequisite Review (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Refractive index defines how light slows down.
We model electrons as masses on springs.
Atoms have a natural vibration frequency.
animations: Create text 'Light Interaction' at center, color #FFFFFF.
Fade in simple light ray animation from left.
Add label 'Ray' in #FF00FF near the light ray.
Transition to next slide with wipe effect.

sections.title: The Microscopic Origin (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Oscillating electrons emit a secondary wave.
The result is a refractive index above one.
animations: Visualize atoms as small spheres, color #00FF00.
Show atom vibrating in response to wave, color #FF0000.

sections.title: Color Dependence: Dispersion (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: Light color relates to its frequency.
Oscillation amplitude depends on light frequency.
Resonance occurs near the natural frequency.
animations: Show light splitting into spectrum colors, #FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization & Conclusion (3:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Light enters a prism at an angle.
Colors bend based on their wavelength.
animations: Show mathematical formula for dispersion in #FFFFFF.
